# Textarea

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

forms · tier 1 · beta · renders on the server, with only its interactive part in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For text longer than a line: a message, a bio, a note. It is a native `<textarea>` with the
field look of Input, so it is server HTML, and a form sends what is typed with no script at all.

```tsx
import { Textarea, TextareaSkeleton } from 'topclassui/textarea'
```

```tsx
<label htmlFor="bio">About you</label>
<Textarea id="bio" name="bio" rows={3} maxLength={500} aria-describedby="bio-hint" />
<span id="bio-hint">A short paragraph is enough</span>
<Textarea aria-label="Notes" name="notes" autosize maxRows={10} showCount />
```

**A name is required.** Pass `id` (for a `<label htmlFor>`), `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`;
the type refuses a Textarea with none of the three.

**`maxLength` is 5000 by default.** Pass your own number, or `maxLength={null}` for no cap. It is
the native `maxlength`, so the browser stops typing and pasting there.

**`autosize` and `showCount` load a small client half.** Without them a Textarea renders no client
code. With `autosize` the rows follow the text from `rows` up to `maxRows`, then it scrolls; the
server counts line breaks, so a long first line that wraps grows once the page hydrates. `maxRows`
alone grows nothing: `autosize` is the switch. The counter reads `42 / 500` under the field, at the
inline end, and is the field's description: always with `showCount`, and with `autosize` alone from
nine tenths of the cap. At the cap it turns bold; that is not an error.

**The width** is an Input's (`--tc-input-width`), and less in a narrow row. `fullWidth` fills the
container. With `autosize` or `showCount` the width belongs to the box around the textarea, and a
width class in `className` lands on the textarea inside it: use `fullWidth`, or size the parent.

**`dir` is yours.** `dir="auto"` lets each text take the direction of its first letter.

**Typed before hydration.** With no script, what is typed is kept and sent. When the script arrives
late, React 19 puts a textarea that has a default back to that default as it hydrates (on every
textarea of the page, not only this one); a field with no default keeps what was typed.

**A form reset is native**, and the counter and the rows follow it. A button with `id="reset"` or
`name="reset"` inside a form hides `form.reset` and breaks React's own reset.

**`TextareaSkeleton`** is the box of the field: give it the same `size`, `fullWidth` and `rows`.

**A parent that clips** (`overflow-hidden`) needs 4px of padding, or it cuts the focus ring off.

### Not built

The `variant` prop (one is drawn), a live region for the counter, a counter on a Textarea with no
client half, a count by grapheme (it counts UTF-16 code units, as `maxlength` does), danger at the
limit, a check written with `zod/mini`. Two clauses of Phase 4 wait for a Field: a Textarea in a
server Field posted with JavaScript off, and the same with `FormAction` and `FieldLive`.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import { Textarea } from 'topclassui/textarea'
```

## Props

Required: `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` or `id`. Every other prop below is optional.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-label` | **yes**, or `aria-labelledby` or `id` | `string` | - | The name read out when no visible label names the control. |
| `aria-labelledby` | **yes**, or `aria-label` or `id` | `string` | - | The id of the visible text that names the control. |
| `id` | **yes**, or `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` | `string` | - | The id a `<label htmlFor>` points at. |
| `autosize` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Grows with the text from rows up to maxRows once the page has hydrated; loads the small client half. |
| `fullWidth` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Stretches the textarea, and the box around it with autosize or showCount, to the width of its container. |
| `invalid` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the value as wrong: sets aria-invalid, and the border turns to danger and thickens. |
| `maxLength` | no | `unknown` | `5000` | The character cap: your number, 5000 by default, or null for none; clamped to 0-2147483647 and rounded down. |
| `maxRows` | no | `integer`, min 1, max 40 | `6` | With autosize, the most lines it grows to before it scrolls; clamped to 1-40 and never under rows. |
| `rows` | no | `integer`, min 1, max 40 | `3` | The lines it shows, and the least it shrinks to with autosize; clamped to 1-40. |
| `showCount` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Always shows the count against the cap under the field; with autosize alone it shows from nine tenths of it. |
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | The shared control scale: the padding and the type step. custom emits no size classes. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
